PullRequest.Title: Add sandbox policy reports to Copilot agent sessions
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/42182471-09a8-46b9-b2e5-a9480c932864

Add `/sandbox-policy` to Copilot agent-host sessions. The VS Code command invokes the SDK's existing `/sandbox policy` command and presents its effective policy as a persisted Markdown report, without starting a model turn or changing sandbox enforcement.

## User experience

- Offer `/sandbox-policy` in slash-command completion while keeping native `/sandbox` subcommands hidden.
- Show an **Open Sandbox Policy** link in the response that opens the formatted report in Markdown preview.
- Use normal theme-aware chat link colors, including hover and active states.
- Support mouse, Enter, and Space activation, with accessible-help guidance.
- Save a unique report for each invocation so earlier links continue to show their original snapshots.

## Implementation

- Introduce optional host-side `getInvocation` and `getOutput` hooks on resolved slash commands, separate from SDK catalog metadata. Omitted hooks or hooks returning `undefined` preserve the existing SDK invocation and output behavior.
- Support structured text and link output with optional Markdown and preview flags. Keep command lifecycle, mode handling, and runtime-settings invalidation in the session.
- Keep sandbox-specific argument validation, SDK mapping, policy formatting, and report persistence in `CopilotSandboxPolicyDisplay`.
- Strip ANSI styling, preserve SDK Markdown, format recognized terminal policy reports, and safely fence unrecognized plain text. Propagate invocation and file-write failures instead of emitting broken links.
- Preserve preview metadata across local and remote Agent Host URI rewriting without passing it to filesystem providers.
- Extract a reusable single-anchor rendering helper to avoid a second anchor scan. Repeated decoration does not register duplicate widgets or listeners.
- Reuse the shared SDK command type in completion handling.

## Compatibility

- Existing commands retain their default invocation and rendering when no custom behavior applies.
- Preserve native sandbox aliases and raw SDK input; do not format unrelated sandbox subcommands or client commands as policy reports.
- Reserve the host alias against runtime name collisions and keep it discoverable when SDK command discovery fails.
- No SDK dependency changes, new permissions, or sandbox-policy enforcement changes.

## Validation

- **803 targeted tests passed** across Copilot session, command-handler, completion, Markdown rendering, inline-anchor, URI adapter, and accessibility-help suites.
- Regression coverage includes local/remote preview links, rich links enabled/disabled, keyboard activation, report formatting and persistence, error propagation, optional-hook fallbacks, and duplicate-widget prevention.
- A 1,001-link regression test verifies a single anchor scan with 1,000 ordinary links and one preview link.
- Core typecheck and transpile watchers completed with zero errors.
- ESLint passed for changed refactor files; CSS lint passed with only pre-existing design-token suggestions.
- Dark and light Component Explorer fixtures render without errors; preview-link colors were checked against regular chat links.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke /sandbox-policy in a Copilot agent-host session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Command resolution is local for the reserved alias; mode application and one SDK commands.invoke call must complete, followed by policy formatting and one awaited file write before the link response is emitted.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the SDK's existing sandbox policy command
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one invocation per accepted /sandbox-policy request; no collection fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The host alias did not exist; other runtime slash commands already used one SDK invoke call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the command response until the SDK returns the policy.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write one Markdown policy snapshot under the session data directory
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file write per successful explicit command invocation, with a unique UUID path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No sandbox-policy snapshot was written because the host alias and report feature did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before emitting the report link, preventing a link to an incomplete file.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of explicit /sandbox-policy invocations and size of the SDK policy text; expected policy output is small and each invocation creates one snapshot.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No batching or coalescing is used; each accepted user invocation performs its own SDK call and write. Normal session command handling governs concurrent turns.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Command resolution bypasses runtime discovery for the reserved alias. Policy output is intentionally not cached so each link preserves its invocation-time snapshot.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the one-call/one-write critical path from the changed code and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users could invoke the command repeatedly, but snapshots are small, explicitly requested, and removed with session data; no realistic high-impact growth was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added boundary work is necessary, bounded per explicit user action, and retained files have session-scoped cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Request slash-command completions and resolve runtime commands
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cold completion may wait up to the existing caller-supplied command-list timeout; warm completion uses the existing in-memory catalog. The built-in sandbox-policy entry is prepended locally.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One in-flight coalesced request per cache lifetime; subsequent callers share the promise or cached catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cached/coalesced SDK command-list call already powered completion and resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold discovery may affect completion availability up to maxWaitMs; the host alias remains available even if discovery fails.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Runtime command catalog size and completion keystroke frequency; filtering/prepending is linear in the small catalog while boundary work remains coalesced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing inFlight promise coalesces concurrent catalog requests; cache invalidation starts a fresh generation without joining stale work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold cache performs one SDK list; warm cache reuses the catalog. Failure clears the empty cache as before, while the local alias is still returned.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from provider cache implementation and changed call sites.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog size is not measured, but no new per-command boundary or loss of coalescing was introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: only small local array/filter work was added and the expensive SDK boundary retains its existing cache and coalescing behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or restore chat Markdown containing sandbox policy links and ordinary links
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Markdown rendering synchronously scans anchors once and identifies preview metadata. Creating each preview widget starts an asynchronous file stat that is not awaited by rendering; ordinary links perform no filesystem operation. Incremental streaming rerenders repeat the existing full Markdown pipeline on rAF batches.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat the linked resource when constructing the InlineAnchorWidget
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One asynchronous stat per newly rendered preview link; effective count equals the number of policy links in the rendered response/history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Sandbox policy links did not exist and ordinary Markdown links were not converted into this widget by the decoration pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The promise is not awaited, so it does not block initial rendering; it can later refresh file/folder icon classes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of anchors in one Markdown part, number of query-bearing links, streaming rerender batches, and number of persisted policy-link responses restored.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Anchor inspection is synchronous and serial in one DOM scan; file stats are launched asynchronously per preview widget with no explicit limiter, but realistic preview-link cardinality is the number of explicit policy invocations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Already-rendered anchors are detected by class within a render. Full rerenders dispose registrations and recreate DOM/widgets; there is no stat cache in the widget.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added per-anchor metadata check and one asynchronous stat per preview widget; low evidence of material user-visible cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The synthetic 1,001-link test proves linear scanning but does not establish a realistic latency regression; normal policy-link cardinality is expected to be very low.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the implementation avoids a second anchor scan, performs only linear lightweight checks for ordinary links, and preview-link filesystem work is low-cardinality and off the render critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rewrite and open local or remote Agent Host policy report links
Scenarios.CriticalPath: URI/query rewriting is synchronous during Markdown link transformation and performs no I/O. On explicit mouse or keyboard activation, the opener reads the target through the applicable file provider and opens the Markdown preview editor.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open/read the generated policy report through the local or Agent Host file provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One opener request per user activation; no per-anchor eager read is added by query rewriting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no generated policy report link; normal file anchors already used the same opener path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only blocks the user-requested editor open, not chat rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of explicit link activations; URI query manipulation is constant work per transformed internal link.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each activation independently calls the opener; no background burst or collection fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No policy-content cache is added at the UI layer; the persisted snapshot is read through existing file-provider/editor caching behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from URI rewrite and widget click paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency depends on local versus remote Agent Host transport, but it occurs only after explicit activation and once per activation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: metadata preservation adds only bounded CPU work and the expensive read remains user-triggered with cardinality one.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 19 changed files and all diff pages. Traced command discovery/invocation, snapshot persistence and cleanup, remote URI rewriting, Markdown rendering, widget disposal, and file-opening boundaries. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
